input.content:
What a dental practice site actually needs to do

Most people who land on your website aren't browsing — they're deciding whether to book. They want to know, in about ten seconds, whether you take their insurance, where you're located, whether you have appointments this week, and whether other patients trust you. If your site loads slowly, looks dated, or buries that information behind three clicks, they'll open a new tab and call the next dentist on the list instead.

That's the bar: fast, professional, mobile-friendly, and organized around what a nervous or busy patient actually wants to find. You don't need a flashy site. You need the right sections, done well, live today instead of "sometime next quarter" once a web designer gets to it.

The sections your practice site can't skip

Services

List what you actually do — cleanings, whitening, crowns, Invisalign, emergency care, pediatric dentistry, whatever applies. Vague copy like "comprehensive dental care" doesn't help patients or search engines. Name the procedures. Patients searching "emergency tooth extraction near me" need to see that phrase, or something close to it, on your site.

About / meet the dentist

A short bio, a real photo, credentials, and how long you've been practicing. Dental visits are personal and a little nerve-wracking for a lot of people — a face and a few sentences of context do more to build trust than another stock photo of a smiling model.

Location and hours

Full address, a map, parking notes if relevant, and hours that are correct and easy to scan. This sounds obvious, but it's the single most common thing broken or out of date on small-practice websites.

Appointment request

A simple form where a patient enters their name, contact info, preferred day/time, and reason for the visit. Kodely can build you a genuinely good-looking, professional appointment-request page and contact form. To be clear about what that means today: it collects the request and sends it to you — it does not yet sync automatically to a calendar or scheduling system. Most small practices are fine with this as a starting point: the request comes in, your front desk confirms by phone or email, same as an inquiry from any other channel.

Patient reviews

A dedicated section with a handful of real testimonials, plus a clear link out to your Google Business Profile where the full review history lives. Reviews are one of the biggest trust signals for a first-time patient, and they help local search too.

A prompt you can copy and use right now

Kodely builds from plain-English descriptions typed into a chat box — the more specific you are, the better the first draft. Here's an example for a fictional practice, Willow Creek Dental, that you can adapt with your own details:

Prompt: "Build a website for Willow Creek Dental, a family dentistry practice in Bend, Oregon. We offer general checkups and cleanings, teeth whitening, Invisalign, and emergency dental care. Use a clean, calming design in soft blues and white, with a warm, welcoming feel — not clinical or cold. Include a homepage with a hero section and a clear call-to-action to request an appointment, a Services section listing our four services with short descriptions, an About section introducing Dr. Elena Marsh with a short bio, a Location and Hours section with our address (412 Larch Street, Bend, OR) and Monday-Friday 8am-5pm hours, an appointment request form asking for name, phone, email, preferred date, and reason for visit, and a Patient Reviews section with three sample testimonials. Make it fully mobile-friendly."

That single prompt is usually enough for a solid first version. From there you keep chatting: "make the hero image bigger," "add a Insurance We Accept section," "change the accent color to teal" — each change edits the real components Kodely already generated, and you can preview the result immediately.

What you actually get when it's done

  • Real code, not a template. Kodely generates an actual Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS app with its own component files — a genuine foundation you can keep building on, not a locked-down theme with swapped colors.
  • Live preview as you build. You see the actual compiled site update while you describe changes, not a mockup.
  • A free live URL. One click publishes your site to willowcreekdental.kodely.site (or your practice's name) — included at no extra cost. There's no custom-domain support yet, so for now your site lives at that address.
  • Checkpoints. Every successful generation is a save point. If a change doesn't look right, roll back for free and try a different instruction.
  • Code view. You can see and copy the generated source directly in the app. Full project export as a downloadable zip isn't available yet.
  • Ongoing edits by chat. Adding a new service, updating your hours, swapping a testimonial — all done by describing the change, no code editor required.

Tips for local SEO once your site is live

  • Keep your name, address, and phone number identical everywhere they appear — your website, Google Business Profile, and any directory listings. Inconsistent details hurt local rankings.
  • Claim and fully fill out your Google Business Profile and link to it from your site. For most dental searches, this listing gets seen before the website does.
  • Use the actual service names patients search for — "dental implants," "root canal," "same-day crowns" — in your Services section headings, not just marketing language.
  • Mention your city and neighborhood in the copy, not just the address block. "Family dentist in Bend, Oregon" reads naturally and helps local search understand what you do and where.
  • Make sure it's fast and mobile-friendly. A large share of "dentist near me" searches happen on a phone, often from someone already in pain — a slow site loses that visitor immediately.
  • Ask happy patients for reviews and keep the testimonials on your site current. Fresh, specific reviews (not generic ones) perform better with both patients and search engines.

FAQ

Can Kodely build online booking for my dental practice?

Kodely can build a professional, well-designed appointment-request page and contact form. It collects the patient's request — it doesn't yet connect to a real calendar or scheduling backend automatically, so your team confirms the appointment manually, the same way you'd handle a phone or email inquiry.

Can I use my own domain, like willowcreekdental.com?

Not yet. Right now every published site lives at a free yourname.kodely.site address. Custom domain support isn't available yet.

Do I need to know how to code?

No. You describe what you want in plain English, and Kodely writes and updates the actual code for you. If you're curious, you can open the code view to see and copy the generated source, but it's never required.

How much does it cost to build a dentist website with Kodely?

New accounts get 750 free credits with no card required, and a typical first build for a site like this runs roughly 100-150 credits — enough for several iterations while you get the sections right. If you need more, top-ups start at $9 for 500 credits, with a $40 pack for 2,500 credits and a $90 pack for 6,000 credits; credits never expire. Builds that fail to compile aren't charged. See pricing for full details.

Can I export the code and host it myself?

Not yet — there's no zip download or export option today. You can view and copy source from the in-app code view, and publish directly to your free kodely.site address.

How do I get started?

Create a free account at sign up — no card required — and describe your practice the way it's shown in the example prompt above. If you already have an account, log in and start a new project. For more examples and tips, browse the blog, or head to the homepage to see what else Kodely can build.
